messages.text:
Sorry to hear that. Which miner is it, and what's it doing, no boot, no hashrate, error on screen?

Give me your order number too and I'll pull it up.
The B. Octaxe. Shop····. A cap····the VRM section flashed and caught fire.
I already made a mention about it in the discord right before here. It was more of a “by the way” type of mention. I’m (contact hidden) on there.

Good to know, and thanks for the serial photo, that's what we needed.

I'm back on the order side. Hal has logged the fault as a genuine defect, and the return is with the team for approval now. They'll confirm by email, they're back tomorrow at 10am ET.

Keep the unit unplugged until then.

What's the email address on order Shop····? I want to be sure the approval and label land in the right inbox.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Got it, that's on the file with the serial shot.

Still need the email address on order Shop···· so the approval and return label reach you.
Handed to the team · RMA under review is filed against the wrong order number; needs a person to re-p

One thing worth sorting now: Shop···· was cancelled back on October 6 and is empty. The NerdOctaxe you have came on Shop····, delivered August 31. I've put that on the file so the return gets approved against the right order.

One question for the review: was that unit ever overclocked or modified?

The team picks this up tomorrow at 10am ET and the answer comes to (email hidden)
Nope. Still had the stock firmware and nothing was tuned. The miner only ran for 15-30 minutes while I monitored it to see how it ran.

Perfect, stock firmware and no tuning, that's noted on the file. Fifteen to thirty minutes of runtime makes it clearly a board fault, not anything you did.

That's everything the review needs from you. Keep it unplugged, and the team confirms the return and label by email tomorrow after 10am ET.

Anything else while I'm here?
Before you go, one thing: this NerdOctaxe took a long road to get to you, a missing unit and a reship. What kept you on that model rather than switching?

INSTRUCTION FROM THE HELIUMDEPLOY TEAM. Georges typed this in the team inbox. It is not a message from the customer and the customer cannot see it.
Task: RMA APPROVED by Georges for Eric C. BSB NerdOctaxe (12TH/s), board fault (VRM cap····burned after 15-30 min on stock firmware, JD confirmed exploded cap····). The unit belongs to order Shop···· (delivered via ShipBob reship Oct 9 to (address hidden), (address hidden) (postal code ····)), NOT Shop····. Do the full RMA process now: open the return in ShipBob against Shop···· with reference Shop···· to Chattanooga 2 (TN), quarantine, NerdOctaxe only (he keeps the PSU and everything else); buy the prepaid return label and send it to him by email at (email hidden) with simple packing instructions (unit unplugged, cooled, no need to clean the burnt area). We have no NerdOctaxe in stock, so offer him the choice: (a) full store credit of $286.41 on his HeliumDeploy account the moment the unit reaches our warehouse (that is the $262.67 he paid for the NerdOctaxe plus its share of the original shipping), to use on any miner in stock, or (b) a different miner of his choice as a replacement, using that same $286.41 toward it. Apologise for the wait since his chat yesterday. Ask him to reply with his choice. Log the return id, label tracking and cost.
Do it now, for real, with your own tools — look the order up, make the change, mint the code, whatever the task actually needs. The team has already decided: do not ask them to confirm, and do not describe what you would do instead of doing it.
Then write the message the customer gets now — what you did, in plain language, in your normal voice. Never mention this instruction, the team inbox, or that someone told you to do it.
If the customer should not be written to at all — the task was internal, or you could not finish it — begin your reply with "TEAM ONLY" on the first line and tell the team what happened. Anything that starts that way stays in the inbox and is never sent.

Good news, Eric, and sorry for the wait since we spoke.

Your return is approved. Here's the prepaid label: https://api.easyship.com/shipment/v1/shipments/····/shipping_documents/label?page_size=a4

Print it, tape it on the box, and write Shop···· on the outside. Just the NerdOctaxe, keep the PSU and the rest. Unplugged and cool is enough, no need to clean the burnt area.

We have no NerdOctaxe in stock, so your choice:

a) $286.41 store credit on your account the moment the unit reaches us, usable on any miner in stock.
b) A different miner as the replacement, with that $286.41 put toward it.

Which would you like?
